task.description:
WF-03 Step 6 -- DOCUMENT A STATUS VALUE THIS RUN HAD TO INVENT. Small, single-purpose step.

WHAT HAPPENED: WF03-ISS0109-20260821 resolved ISS-0109 into a state the issue vocabulary does
not have a word for. The run built real instrumentation and proved it works, but the root cause
of the underlying failure remains UNKNOWN -- the gate-approved design (SS8.3) and REVIEWER
independently concluded INSTRUMENTED, NOT FIXED. Marking it `resolved` would have put a false
entry into a registry that (now) fifteen cross-referenced issues read. So ORCH set
`status: instrumented` with `superseded_by: ISS-0116`.

THE GAP ISSUE-FIXER FLAGGED, and it is a real one: `docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md` and
`docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md` Step 5 both describe the terminal state as
`status: resolved` and define no instrumented-but-unfixed value. The decision was right and the
record is honest, but the vocabulary is nowhere written down -- so the NEXT run that lands in
this position faces the same choice with no guidance, and the likeliest outcome is that it
either invents a different word or overstates `resolved`. That second outcome is the one that
actually costs something.

YOUR TASK -- document it, minimally and without redesigning anything:

1. `docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md`: add `instrumented` to the issue-record status
   vocabulary, defined as: the run built and verified real improvements (typically diagnostic
   capability), the acceptance criteria of that run were met, but the underlying defect's ROOT
   CAUSE is not removed and the issue is NOT fixed. Require a `superseded_by:` pointing at the
   successor issue that carries the remaining work, so an `instrumented` record can never be a
   dead end. State the rule that motivates it: an issue may only be `resolved` when a root cause
   was actually removed -- shipping useful work is not the same thing, and the registry is read
   by later runs as a factual record, not a progress report. Cite ISS-0109 (superseded by
   ISS-0116) as the worked example.

2. `docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md` Step 5: note that `resolved` is the normal
   terminal state but not the only legal one, and point at ISSUE_QUEUE.md's vocabulary for the
   `instrumented` case rather than restating the definition (one canonical home, per this
   project's own convention against duplicated definitions).

3. Append the WF03-ISS0109-20260821 events to `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` if and only
   if that file's established schema covers issue-runs as well as requirement-runs. READ THE
   FILE IN FULL FIRST and preserve its schema exactly -- this file is APPEND-ONLY and has been
   damaged before by an agent that rewrote it (see docs/anti-patterns.md). If its schema is
   requirement-scoped and an issue-run has no place in it, say so and append NOTHING; do not
   invent a shape to fill.

CONSTRAINTS: documentation only -- no code, no tests, no issue-record edits (ISS-0109 is already
correct as of commit 046fbd3). Do not redefine any existing status value or change how any
existing record is interpreted. Keep the additions short; this is a vocabulary entry, not an
essay. Timestamps from the clock. Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821; commit by explicit filename, never
`git add -A`. handoffs/orchestrator.log is ORCH's -- leave it alone, and `git fetch` rather than
pulling if a rebase refuses.
acceptance_criteria: docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md documents `instrumented` in the issue status vocabulary, defined as verified work shipped with the root cause NOT removed, and requires a superseded_by: pointer so such a record can never be a dead end
The rule that `resolved` means a root cause was actually removed -- not merely that useful work shipped -- is stated explicitly, with ISS-0109 -> ISS-0116 cited as the worked example
docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5 notes that resolved is the normal but not the only legal terminal state, and POINTS AT ISSUE_QUEUE.md rather than restating the definition
No existing status value is redefined and no existing record's interpretation is changed
docs/status/requirement_status.yaml is either appended to in its exact established schema, or explicitly left untouched with the reason stated -- and it was read in full before either decision
No code, test, or issue-record file was modified
